macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. retail sales fall 0.6% in July, pointing to slower consumer spending
items.summary: U.S. retail sales posted their first decline in nine months, dropping 0.6% in July after a revised 0.2% gain in June. Reuters said the report suggests a marked slowdown in consumer spending at the start of the third quarter.

items.title: Markets price out some Fed tightening after weak U.S. data
items.summary: A market wrap noted that weak retail sales and softer consumer sentiment reduced the odds of a September Federal Reserve rate hike to 29% from 35% on Thursday. The dollar weakened and Treasury yields moved lower on the data.

items.title: Inflation data shows cooling price pressures in the U.S.
items.summary: Recent U.S. inflation data showed annual inflation at 3.4% in July, slightly below the prior month. July CPI developments helped ease immediate concerns about another Fed rate hike.

items.title: U.S. consumer sentiment slips in early August
items.summary: The University of Michigan's preliminary August consumer sentiment index fell to 51.0 from 55.2 in July, reinforcing signs of weaker household confidence. The softer reading contributed to the pullback in rate-hike expectations.

items.title: Gold holds recent gains as Fed hike odds fade
items.summary: Gold prices stayed supported as market expectations for another Fed rate hike eased following the latest inflation data. The report said headline inflation held at 3.4% and core CPI eased to 2.5%.

items.title: U.S. equity futures and major indexes end nearly flat after economic data
items.summary: A Reuters-linked market snapshot showed the S&P 500 up 0.10% and the Dow down 0.04% late in the session, suggesting a muted response in U.S. equities. Broader market moves were dominated by the retail sales and inflation data.

items.title: Oil rises as markets watch geopolitical tensions and Fed outlook
items.summary: Global markets saw oil prices rise by more than $1 a barrel while U.S. and European shares fell, according to a market report. The move came as investors weighed U.S.-Iran tensions and weaker expectations for further Fed tightening.

items.title: India wholesale inflation eases, but price pressures remain elevated
items.summary: Indian wholesale inflation eased to 9.8% in July, though reports said price pressures may stay elevated through FY27. Fuel and power inflation also moderated from the prior month.

items.title: Anima Holding reports half-year 2026 results
items.summary: Anima Holding said half-year 2026 sales were €222.5 million, revenue was €286.8 million, and net income was €158.8 million. The results drew fresh attention in company-level market news.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA reportedly sells for $55 billion in Saudi-led buyout
items.summary: BBC says Electronic Arts, the maker of The Sims and EA FC, is being taken private in a $55 billion deal led by a Saudi-backed group. The transaction would significantly reshape one of gaming’s biggest publishers and adds substantial debt to the company.

items.title: Xbox Series X prices rise in the UK amid memory chip cost pressure
items.summary: BBC reports that Xbox console prices in the UK have increased sharply, with one model up by 43%. The price hike is tied to rising memory chip costs and broader hardware cost pressures affecting the industry.

items.title: Roblox faces Senate subcommittee investigation over child safety
items.summary: The Verge reports that a Senate subcommittee has opened an investigation into Roblox focused on child safety concerns. The inquiry adds fresh regulatory pressure on the popular user-generated gaming platform.

items.title: Netflix reportedly shutters Night School Studio and another gaming team
items.summary: Recent reporting says Netflix is closing Night School Studio, the Oxenfree developer it acquired in 2021, and also winding down Moonloot. The move suggests a pullback from Netflix’s broader gaming efforts.

items.title: Amazon to hand Lost Ark Western operations back to Smilegate
items.summary: A report says Amazon will transfer live Western operations for Lost Ark to Smilegate in early 2027. The shift would consolidate control of the MMORPG under its original developer after Amazon’s retreat from MMO publishing.

items.title: Sony takes a major Bungie write-down as live-service strategy changes
items.summary: TipRanks says Sony Interactive Entertainment recorded a ¥120.1 billion, or about $765 million, write-down on Bungie. The move comes as Bungie continues restructuring and as Sony scales back some live-service ambitions.

items.title: Microsoft’s next Xbox plans reportedly take shape
items.summary: TipRanks reports that details are emerging about Microsoft’s next Xbox console, codenamed Project Helix. The system is said to emphasize backward compatibility across multiple Xbox generations.

items.title: Nioh 3 gets a 2026 release window with a playable PS5 demo
items.summary: The Gameer says Nioh 3 is coming in 2026 and that players can try a demo on PS5 now. The announcement makes it one of the biggest action-RPG reveals in the latest wave of game news.

items.title: Pokémon Gamma Emerald launches in early access
items.summary: GamingBible reports that Pokémon Gamma Emerald has launched in early access. The fan project is being positioned as a must-play for fans of Generation 3-era Pokémon.

items.title: Game Kitchen teases a key date for Ninja Gaiden fans
items.summary: GameRant says The Game Kitchen revealed an important July 31 date for Ninja Gaiden fans during Sony’s State of Play. The update suggests another notable franchise development tied to the showcase cycle.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Waymo gets approval to expand robotaxi service across 18 California counties
items.summary: California regulators approved Waymo’s biggest expansion yet, allowing the company to operate across 18 counties from Sonoma to San Diego. The move significantly broadens the reach of its autonomous ride-hailing service in the state.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly trims a massive funding guarantee tied to an OpenAI data center
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia has scaled back plans for a $250 billion guarantee for an OpenAI data center project in Ohio. Reuters separately reported similar developments, highlighting continued volatility around large AI infrastructure financing deals.

items.title: Apple asks court for a 15% cut on purchases made outside the App Store
items.summary: Apple is seeking permission to charge commissions of up to 15% on purchases made through external links in iOS apps. The proposal is part of the company’s ongoing legal and policy fight over App Store billing rules.

items.title: Self-driving trucks begin testing on California highways
items.summary: Aurora Innovation and Kodiak AI received permits from the California Department of Motor Vehicles to test autonomous trucks on public highways. The approvals mark a notable step forward for commercial trucking automation.

items.title: Google adds a toggle to remove visible watermarks from AI-generated media
items.summary: Google is allowing users in Gemini and Flow to remove visible watermarks from AI-generated images, videos, and music. According to the reporting, SynthID watermarks and C2PA metadata remain embedded.

items.title: OpenAI launches a new macOS activity timeline feature
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Computer History, an opt-in feature that turns day-to-day macOS activity into a timeline that ChatGPT and Codex can use. The feature appears aimed at making past computer actions easier to search and reuse.

items.title: OpenAI previews an Ultrafast API tier powered by Cerebras
items.summary: OpenAI launched a preview of Ultrafast, an API tier using Cerebras hardware that reportedly runs GPT-5.6 Sol up to 14 times faster and generates up to 750 output tokens per second. The release appears designed to attract enterprise users needing lower latency.

items.title: US courts plan to publish how often spyware is authorized in investigations
items.summary: The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts told TechCrunch it will begin disclosing how often judges authorize spyware use to wiretap suspected criminals. The change would add more transparency to a little-reported investigative tool.
